realtime_tracking_note: The goal is in-line, time-resolved tracking of composition during extrusion; acquisition speed and synchronisation matter if two methods are later combined.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the melt is clear and the API bands are strong in MIR alone, O1 may suffice; if the melt temperature exceeds probe material limits, the installation concept must change before any method is chosen.
proposal.next_step: Answer the clarification questions and run a multi-method lab trial on representative hot melt samples with MIR-ATR first, then Raman, against the offline assays.

brief_answer: Test MIR-ATR first: it is the only supplied technique with a published precedent for API in hot polymer extrusion, and ATR suits melts in contact with the crystal. Run Raman as a comparison and NIR reflection only if the melt proves opaque; skip NIR transmission, which fails in thick opaque melts. Open points: polymer/API identity and concentration range, melt temperature and pressure, optical regime, required accuracy and response time, and fouling behaviour at the probe port.
